rules: Help/usage text is produced by Python's argparse with default HelpFormatter (Python 3.10-3.12 vintage: header is 'options:', and usage wrap tokens are produced by the old regex splitter so '--a A' splits into '--a' + 'A').

Default (COLUMNS unset / non-tty stdout) help is exactly these 127 bytes: 'usage: test4_executable [-h] --a A --b B --c C

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --a A
  --b B
  --c C
'. Exit 0, stderr empty.

Indentation constants: action lines are indented 2 spaces; the help description for -h starts at 1-based column 15 (2 spaces + '-h, --help' (10 chars) + 2 spaces = offset 14); 'options:' is at column 1; there is exactly one empty line between the usage block and 'options:'; exactly one trailing newline overall; no trailing whitespace anywhere.
--a/--b/--c have no help string, so they are rendered as bare '  --a A' / '  --b B' / '  --c C' with no padding and are NEVER wrapped or reflowed at any width.

width = terminal_columns - 2. terminal_columns = int(os.environ['COLUMNS']) if COLUMNS parses as a Python int and is > 0; otherwise the tty size of the STDOUT file descriptor; otherwise the hard fallback 80. The width source is stdout even when the text is written to stderr.

COLUMNS parsing follows Python int(): optional surrounding whitespace, optional +/- sign, leading zeros, '_' digit separators, and any Unicode decimal digits are accepted. Values that fail to parse, or are <= 0, are ignored (fall through to tty/80). Floats ('40.5') and hex ('0x28') fail to parse.
Usage-line algorithm: build body = prog + ' [-h] --a A --b B --c C'. If 7 + len(body) <= width, emit 'usage: ' + body on one line. Otherwise split into tokens ['[-h]','--a','A','--b','B','--c','C'].

Usage wrap, prog placement: if 7 + len(prog) <= 0.75 * width, prepend prog to the token list, use indent = ' ' * (7 + len(prog) + 1), and strip that indent from the first line (which instead carries the 'usage: ' prefix). Otherwise put prog alone on the first line after 'usage: ' and use indent = ' ' * 7 for every following line.

Usage greedy fill: line_len = 6 (len('usage: ')-1) for the prefixed first line, else len(indent)-1. For each token: if line_len + 1 + len(token) > width AND the current line already has a token, flush the line (indent + ' '.join(tokens)) and reset line_len = len(indent)-1. Then append the token and line_len += 1 + len(token). A single over-long token is emitted on its own line unsplit.

Help-body layout constants for this program: action_max_length = 12 (= 2 + len('-h, --help')); max_help_position = min(24, max(width - 20, 4)); help_position = min(14, max_help_position); action_width = help_position - 4; help_width = max(width - help_position, 11).

If len('-h, --help') = 10 <= action_width, emit '  ' + '-h, --help'.ljust(action_width) + '  ' + first help line, with continuation lines indented help_position spaces. Otherwise emit '  -h, --help\n' and indent every help line by help_position spaces.
Help text 'show this help message and exit' (31 chars) is greedy word-wrapped at help_width; words are never hyphenated or broken.

Concrete COLUMNS thresholds: >=48 usage on one line; >=33 prog stays on the 'usage: ' line with a 24-space hanging indent (<=32 -> prog alone on line 1, 7-space indent); >=36 help text on the same line as '-h, --help' with 14-space continuation indent (<=35 -> own line); >=47 help text unwrapped. Help-line indent for COLUMNS<=35 is min(14, max(COLUMNS-22, 4)), i.e. 4 for COLUMNS<=26 then +1 per column up to 13 at COLUMNS=35.

prog = the substring of argv[0] after the last '/' (POSIX basename without trailing-slash stripping), used verbatim: no symlink/realpath resolution, no extension stripping, no whitespace trimming, spaces/tabs/Unicode preserved. 'dir/', '///' and '' all yield an empty prog, which is dropped from the usage join giving 'usage: [-h] --a A --b B --c C'. The same prog string is reused as the 'PROG: error: ...' prefix.

--help/-h writes only to stdout and exits 0; all argparse errors write only to stderr and exit 2 (stdout empty). Error output is 'usage-block\n' + 'PROG: error: MESSAGE\n' with no blank line between them, and the error message line is never wrapped.

-h/--help short-circuits parsing: required-argument checking, unrecognized-argument checking, and the schedule.every().monday.at() call all never run. It works in any argv position and alongside invalid values.

'--' terminates option processing, so '-h' after '--' is not help. Unambiguous long prefixes (--h, --he, --hel) ARE help; matching is case-sensitive. '--help=X' / '-h=1' are errors ('argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument'); '-hh' is accepted as a cluster of two -h.
When both a required-args error and an unrecognized-args error apply, argparse reports the required-args error (required checking happens inside parse_known_args, before the leftover check).
surprises: Usage wrapping splits an option from its metavar: the wrap tokens are '--a' and 'A' separately, not '--a A'. At COLUMNS<=13 the usage really prints '--a' and 'A' on separate lines. A naive port that keeps '--a A' atomic will differ at COLUMNS 10-13 and elsewhere.

The magic 0.75 float comparison decides whether prog shares the 'usage:' line. It is 7 + len(prog) <= 0.75 * width with real float math, so prog length 51 fits at width 78 (58 <= 58.5) but 52 does not. Integer-rounding this comparison gives wrong output at the boundary.

The continuation indent for the -h help text is NOT a constant: it slides from 4 to 14 as COLUMNS goes from <=26 up to 36, via max_help_position = min(24, max(width-20, 4)). Most ports hard-code 24/14 and get every narrow width wrong.

help_width has a hard floor of 11 and help_position a hard floor of 4, so output stops changing below COLUMNS=14 and is identical for COLUMNS=1..13 (including COLUMNS=0/negative being treated as unset).

There are two different single-line thresholds that do not coincide: at COLUMNS=47 the help text is already unwrapped but the usage line is still wrapped. Assuming one 'wide enough' threshold is wrong.

COLUMNS is parsed with Python int(), so '4_0', ' 40 ', '+40', '040', fullwidth '４０' (U+FF14 U+FF10) and Arabic-Indic '٤٠' all mean 40. JS parseInt/Number semantics differ on every one of these, and Number('0x28')=40 would wrongly succeed where Python's int() fails.
COLUMNS<=0 (including 0 and negatives) is silently ignored rather than clamped, falling back to the tty size or 80.
The terminal width always comes from STDOUT's fd, even for the usage block written to STDERR. Redirecting stdout to a file while stderr is a 30-column tty yields 80-column error output.
The 'PROG: error: ...' line is never wrapped, even at COLUMNS=1, while the usage block above it is. Wrapping the whole stderr blob is wrong.

prog comes from argv[0] with no symlink resolution and no trailing-slash stripping: a symlink shows the link's own name, and argv[0]='dir/' or '///' yields an EMPTY prog, producing 'usage: [-h] --a A --b B --c C' with a single space after 'usage:' (the empty component is dropped from the join, not rendered as a double space).

-h wins over everything, including '--help=x'-style errors elsewhere in argv, required-arg errors, and even bogus --a values; but '--help=x' itself is an error with exit 2. '-h x' exits 0 while '-- -h' exits 2.

Writing help to a full/unwritable stdout turns exit 0 into exit 120 with an 'Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>' + 'OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device' block on stderr — a JS port that ignores write errors will report 0.
The section header is 'options:' (Python 3.10+), not 'optional arguments:' — and there is no ANSI color even with FORCE_COLOR/CLICOLOR_FORCE, so this is not 3.14-era argparse.
